en.title: Obsession Star Inde Navarrette Would 'Die Inside' for a Resident Evil Role
en.summary: Fresh off terrifying audiences in 'Obsession,' actress Inde Navarrette reveals her deep love for the iconic 'Resident Evil' franchise. The rising star expressed a fervent desire to join the horror universe, stating she would be overcome with emotion.
en.body:
Inde Navarrette, who recently chilled viewers to the bone in the hit horror film **Obsession**, has made it clear that her interests extend far beyond the silver screen. In a recent interview with Variety, the actress shared her profound admiration for the **Resident Evil** universe, a sentiment that will undoubtedly resonate with the game's massive global fanbase. Navarrette confessed that she is currently deeply immersed in the series, describing herself as being "on a Resident Evil kick." This personal connection to the survival horror genre, coupled with her acting prowess, has fueled speculation and excitement among fans about a potential crossover.

Navarrette's gaming journey began with childhood favorites like **Shrek: Super Party** on PlayStation 2, a gift from her mother, while her father was a fan of the **Call of Duty** series. Today, her gaming palette has expanded to include critically acclaimed titles such as **God of War Ragnarök**, and of course, the terrifying world of **Resident Evil**. When asked if she had been approached for any video game acting roles, Navarrette revealed that she has indeed received offers and is preparing to embark on that new creative path soon. She expressed a desire to start with smaller, independent projects to "test the waters," indicating a thoughtful approach to her burgeoning video game career.

## A Dream Role in Raccoon City

However, it's her specific desire to be part of the **Resident Evil** franchise that truly stands out. When the interviewer suggested that she would be a perfect fit for the series, Navarrette's enthusiastic response was telling. 

> "I love that world specifically, the Resident Evil world," Navarrette said. "That would be perfect for you," DeNicola said. "I think that would be amazing." "I… would die inside," Navarrette said.

This visceral reaction underscores the depth of her fandom. The idea of embodying a character within the lore of **Resident Evil**, a franchise known for its intricate narratives and terrifying monsters, is clearly a monumental aspiration for the young actress. While she remains tight-lipped about the specifics of her upcoming video game involvement, the dream of seeing her bring her passion and talent to the **Resident Evil** universe is one that many fans will eagerly anticipate.

## Why This Matters to Fans

For dedicated **Resident Evil** fans, the idea of a beloved actor who genuinely loves and understands the franchise stepping into a role is incredibly exciting. It suggests a potential for more authentic and nuanced performances, moving beyond mere casting to a true embodiment of the series' spirit. Navarrette's background, including her mother's influence in introducing her to gaming and her own experience with horror, adds a layer of credibility to her aspirations. Her openness about her gaming habits, like streaming **Call of Duty** while wearing a Toad hat, further endears her to the community. This isn't just another celebrity expressing a passing interest; it's an artist with a demonstrable passion for the medium.

## What's Next

While details surrounding Inde Navarrette's current video game project remain under wraps, her clear ambition to join the **Resident Evil** franchise means fans should keep a close eye on future announcements from Capcom. Her involvement could signal a new wave of talent bringing fresh perspectives to established gaming worlds.

content_raw: Another week, another fun tidbit learned about our new favorite gamer turned movie star, Inde Navarrette, who creeped us all the hell out in the smash-hit horror film Obsession earlier this year. We already marveled at Navarrette cooly streaming her Call of Duty killstreaks on Twitch while wearing a Toad hat , and we were charmed to hear she (in part) learned to build PCs by watching Henry Cavill do it on YouTube. This latest revelation is encouraging, too: Navarrette is a big fan of Resident Evil. Hey, so are we! Celebrities: they're just like us. In a video interview with Variety's Tiana DeNicola, Navarrette talked about the first videogames she ever played—her mom bought her Shrek: Super Party for PlayStation 2 and her dad was a big Call of Duty fan—as well as what games she's playing now, like God of War Ragnarök. Navarrette is also playing horror games these days, which feels appropriate considering how spooky Obsession was, and says she's currently "on a Resident Evil kick." DeNicola asked if Navarrette had been contacted by anyone to do any acting in a videogame. "Yes, and I'm starting my journey with that soon," Navarrette said, and though she wouldn't reveal which game she would be acting in, it sounds like it could be an indie game rather than a triple-A blockbuster. "I want to try something smaller to kind of test the waters," she said, "because videogames are obviously an interest of mine." As for playing a part in a Resident Evil project: "I love that world specifically, the Resident Evil world," Navarrette said. "That would be perfect for you," DeNicola said. "I think that would be amazing." "I… would die inside," Navarrette said. Oddly enough, Navarrette hadn't heard about Zach Cregger's Resident Evil film coming out next month, but seemed delighted at the idea. "I will buy a ticket," Navarrette said. "That's exciting." I have to agree with DeNicola, Navarrette would be a perfect fit for Resident Evil, either in a film or a game. Her performance in Obsession required both the type of heightened emotion and the extreme physicality that would be right at home in Raccoon City. Hopefully Capcom will make it happen someday.
